examples.text: I was not carrying cash, so I wrote a cheque for the amount.
examples.translation: 我没有带现金，所以我写了一张支票。

examples.text: They do not, however, all deal with the same banker, and when A gives a cheque to B, B usually pays it not into the same but into some other bank.
examples.translation: 然而，他们并不都与同一家银行打交道，当 A 给 B 一张支票时，B 通常不是将支票存入同一家银行，而是存入另一家银行。

examples.text: Sometimes abbreviations are used (which would be explained on the statement) and only the last three figures of the cheque number may be given. ‘Sundries’ are cash or cheques paid into the account.
examples.translation: 有时会使用缩写（会在声明中解释），并且只能提供支票号码的最后三位数字。“杂项”是指存入账户的现金或支票。

examples.text: You can avoid dealing with paper cheques — written or printed — by paying your bills online.
examples.translation: 您可以通过在线支付账单来避免处理纸质支票——无论是手写的还是印刷的。

examples.text: The daily cheque clearings began around 1770 when bank clerks met at the Five Bells (a tavern in Lombard Street in the City of London) to exchange all their cheques in one place and settle the balances in cash.
examples.translation: 每日支票结算始于1770年左右，当时银行职员在 Five Bells（伦敦金融城倫巴底街的一家小酒馆）会面，在一个地方兑换所有支票并以现金结算余额。
